title: An Interpretable Stylometric Framework for Early Chinese Buddhist Translator Styles: A Case Study on the Attribution of Disputed Works of An Shigao
abstract: arXiv:2611.13636v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Attributing early Chinese Buddhist translations requires evidence that scholars can trace back to the texts. We develop an interpretable stylometric framework that uses features defined or reviewed by Buddhist philologists, including function characters, sentence formulas, sentence-final characters, sentence length, and part-of-speech n-grams. We construct stylistic profiles from 31 authenticated translations by seven translators from the Eastern Han through the Western Jin, then compare eight disputed texts with An Shigao's profile. Two texts, T1557 and T0101, show the strongest stylistic similarity to the authenticated An Shigao corpus, with scores of 0.783 and 0.687, respectively. The attributions agree with those reported by a published BERT-based approach on the same set of disputed texts. The framework requires no task-specific training and allows scholars to inspect which linguistic features support each proposed attribution.

translated_title: 早期汉译佛典译者风格的可解释文体计量学框架：以安世高存疑著作归属为案例研究
translated_abstract: 早期汉译佛典的作者归属需要学者能够回溯至文本本身的证据。我们开发了一个可解释的文体计量学框架，该框架使用由佛教文献学家定义或审定的特征，包括虚字、句式、句末字、句长和词性n-gram。我们根据从东汉到西晋七位译师的31部确证译作构建了风格特征档案，然后将八部存疑文本与安世高的风格档案进行比较。其中两部文本T1557和T0101与确证的安世高语料库显示出最强的风格相似性，得分分别为0.783和0.687。这些归属结果与已发表的基于BERT的方法在同一批存疑文本上的结果一致。该框架无需针对特定任务的训练，并允许学者检验哪些语言特征支持每一项归属提议。
tldr: 本研究提出了一个基于佛教文献学家审定语言特征的可解释文体计量学框架，无需任务特定训练即可分析早期汉译佛典归属，判定T1557和T0101两部存疑文本与安世高风格最为相似，且结果与基于BERT的方法一致。
en_tdlr: This study proposes an interpretable stylometric framework using philologist-defined linguistic features that requires no task-specific training, identifying T1557 and T0101 as the disputed texts most stylistically similar to An Shigao, with results consistent with a published BERT-based approach.
